review_notes: I read the whole file and the neighbouring localization file. I grepped for downstream uses of the forest and root-address definitions. The file has no simp attributes. Its definitions are `by classical exact ...` wrappers, so simp cannot see through them without unfolding. I did not run Lean. I did not report any loop or competing-rule issues, because there are no simp rules here to compete.

findings.excerpt:
q₀ ∈ finiteShiftGridRootAddresses F ↔
      ∃ p ∈ F, finiteShiftGridRootAddress p = q₀
findings.problem: `finiteShiftGridRootAddresses` is a definition wrapping `F.image`. Simp can only see through it after the definition is unfolded. This iff is the canonical membership characterisation, but it is not tagged `@[simp]`. Goals and hypotheses of the form `q₀ ∈ finiteShiftGridRootAddresses F` therefore stay stuck. The file's own proofs have to apply `Finset.mem_biUnion`/`Finset.mem_image` by hand and build the witness `⟨(depth, q), hp, rfl⟩` manually (lines 77-79, 129-134, and the `rcases Finset.mem_image.mp` steps in the laminarity proof). The lemma is also stated only in `∃ p ∈ F` form, with no companion for the pair `(depth, q)`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `mem_finiteShiftGridRootAddresses`. It is a plain membership iff whose right-hand side is built from `F` and `finiteShiftGridRootAddress` alone, so tagging it adds no loop risk. Optionally also add `@[simp] theorem finiteShiftGridRootAddress_mk (d q) : finiteShiftGridRootAddress (d, q) = q / 2 ^ d := rfl`. Then proofs such as the first part of `finiteShiftGridInterval_mem_completeFiniteShiftGridForest` can become `simp`/`exact ⟨_, hp, rfl⟩` instead of manual `Finset.mem_image.mpr`.
findings.benefit: Downstream users get a one-step normal form for root-address membership. Hand-written `Finset.mem_image` plumbing becomes unnecessary.

findings.excerpt:
exact (finiteShiftGridRootAddresses F).biUnion fun q₀ ↦
    completeFiniteShiftGridTree topScale shift maxDepth q₀
findings.problem: The forest is defined as a `biUnion`, but the file has no membership iff for it, such as `I ∈ completeFiniteShiftGridForest .. F ↔ ∃ q₀ ∈ finiteShiftGridRootAddresses F, I ∈ completeFiniteShiftGridTree .. q₀`. Without one, simp cannot rewrite forest membership, and every consumer repeats `Finset.mem_biUnion` or uses `change` to unfold the definition by hand. Four proofs in this file do `rcases Finset.mem_biUnion.mp hI`. A downstream file needs `change I ∈ (finiteShiftGridRootAddresses F).biUnion (fun q₀ ↦ ...) at hIF` before it can use `Finset.mem_biUnion.mp`. This shows the simp interface is incomplete: the definition leaks into proofs.
findings.proposed_change: After the definition add `@[simp] theorem mem_completeFiniteShiftGridForest {topScale shift maxDepth F I} : I ∈ completeFiniteShiftGridForest topScale shift maxDepth F ↔ ∃ q₀ ∈ finiteShiftGridRootAddresses F, I ∈ completeFiniteShiftGridTree topScale shift maxDepth q₀`. Prove it by `classical; simp [completeFiniteShiftGridForest]` or by `Finset.mem_biUnion`. Use it to shorten `completeFiniteShiftGridTree_subset_forest`, `completeFiniteShiftGridForest_subset_some_root`, `completeFiniteShiftGridForest_length_eq_scale` and the downstream `biUnion_rootSubfamily_eq`. The left-hand side is a single membership atom and the right-hand side uses only the tree and root-address names, so there is no cycle.
findings.benefit: Forest membership gets a canonical, simp-reducible form. The `change ... at` unfolding in downstream files and the repeated `Finset.mem_biUnion` destructuring go away.
